summary: Check whether the engine correctly implements each FAQ ruling in the train set.

incorrect.question: Does Abandoned Hall's ability trigger if the spell is countered?
incorrect.notes: The engine fires the `play-spell`/`play-card` trigger events inside the `playSpell` reducer immediately after `addToChain`, before any player can respond. Countering only sets `countered=true` on the chain item (effect-executor.ts:642-644) and skips its effect at resolution (chain-moves.ts:100), but the play-spell trigger has already fired by then. So Abandoned Hall's ability would still trigger on a countered spell, contrary to rules 419.4.a.1 / 425.1.b.

incorrect.question: Can a unit moved into or away from Abandoned Hall by a spell be chosen?
incorrect.notes: playSpell adds the spell to the chain (cards.ts:783) then immediately fires the play-spell event (cards.ts:792), which pushes Abandoned Hall's triggered ability on top of the spell via addToChain (trigger-runner.ts:291-313). resolveTopItem pops LIFO (chain-state.ts:322-323), so the ability resolves and selects its "here" target BEFORE the spell resolves. Result is inverted from the ruling: a unit the spell moves into Abandoned Hall is not yet there (unchoosable), and a unit the spell moves away is still there (choosable). Per 419.4.a the trigger should fire only after the spell finishes resolving.

incorrect.question: Can a unit replayed here by a spell be chosen by Abandoned Hall's triggered ability?
incorrect.notes: The engine emits the `play-spell` event immediately after `addToChain` (cards.ts:792), i.e. when the spell is placed on the chain, not after it resolves per rule 350.1/419.4.a. `fireTriggers` then appends Abandoned Hall's ability on TOP of the spell, and `resolveTopItem` is LIFO (pop from end), so the trigger resolves and picks its `location: "here"` target BEFORE the spell's effect ever runs. The `"play"` effect case (effect-executor.ts:835) also moves the unit straight to `base` rather than appending it as a pending chain item, so there is no rule-337.1.b append-order finalization at all. Net result: the replayed unit is not on the board when Abandoned Hall's target is chosen — opposite of the official ruling.

incorrect.question: Does the Baron Pit need to be scored to win by conquering?
incorrect.notes: Rule 471.1.b.1 (all battlefields scored → final point, else draw a card) is implemented only in the scorePoint reducer (combat.ts:757-782), which correctly iterates Object.keys(draft.battlefields) and would include the Baron Pit. However, the sibling conquer paths — resolveFullCombat attacker-wins (combat.ts:434-448), the conquerBattlefield move (combat.ts:627-659), and non-combat showdown close (chain-moves.ts:788-794) — all do `player.victoryPoints += 1` and call hasPlayerWon/endGame with no every-battlefield check. A player at match point conquering via combat or the conquerBattlefield action wins outright even if Baron Pit is unscored, contrary to the ruling.

incorrect.question: Can Glasc's Deathknell play a unit to the battlefield where he died?
incorrect.notes: The 323.6 implementation (state-based-checks.ts:303-312) nulls `bf.controller` unconditionally — it never checks for Open State / chain existence / ongoing showdown. In `runStateMaintenance`, `performCleanup` kills Glasc AND nulls the battlefield's controller in the same pass, THEN dispatches the `die` event, so by the time Deathknell fires the battlefield is already uncontrolled. Separately, the `play` effect executor (effect-executor.ts:835-847) hardcodes `targetZoneId: "base"` with no battlefield-destination choice, so even absent the 323.6 bug the unit could not be played to that battlefield.

incorrect.notes: resolveFullCombat is atomic: it computes winner from damage-step survivors alone, then immediately conquers/recalls and clears contested. There is no 466.1.a.1 heal-all step (survivors keep their damage counters), no death-trigger window before result determination (kills go straight to trash without firing Deathknell; sfd-165 also has no abilities[] defined), and no "No Result" outcome or 466.3.d.1 re-staging — CombatResult.winner is only attacker|defender|tie, with both-sides-survive hardcoded to "defender". In this scenario the engine would report attacker conquers (Glasc dead, attackers survive) rather than heal → No Result → second combat.
